script.opening_words: Two guys, same age, 27, same city, same income, both pulling around $58,000 a year. Both opened a brokerage account for the first time in the same week, March of 2009, each with $5,000 they'd scraped together. Both had read the same personal finance article about investing in your 20s. Both were terrified. The market had just collapsed 57%. The news was wall-to-wall disaster. Unemployment was climbing toward 10%. CNBC had started running the word crisis in red letters so
script.ending_words: don't have to be that person. You just have to understand the math clearly enough to act on it when your gut is screaming otherwise. That's the whole thing. The window is open. What you do with it is yours. If this changed how you're thinking about the next few months, drop a comment. I read all of them. Subscribe if you haven't. I'll see you in the next one.
script.analysis: Full 20195 canonical characters read. An urgency essay: two-investor 2009 parable ($18,000 vs $210,000); March 2026 context (Iran strikes, Hormuz, Brent $72 to $118, S&P -4.6% quarter, VIX, Fear & Greed); fear chain and stagflation bear case; 1970s vs today; RBC conflict data; Gulf War, Iraq 2003, WWII; bull/bear statistics and rolling returns; 2009 Amazon/Microsoft/Apple recoveries; 2020 COVID; loss aversion; Dalbar; JPMorgan best days; three-part framework (S&P ETF 40-50%, quality stocks, discipline); dollar safe haven; Goldman target; three options; close. Directly verified (FRED): Brent ~$72 pre-war and $118 on 2026-03-20; S&P Q1 -4.6%; 1975 unemployment 9%; dollar +2.7% in March. Wrong or overstated: VIX "mid-teens to over 35" (closes ~18-21 to 31); "today inflation 2.7%" and "unemployment 4.2%" (latest at upload 2.4% and 4.4%); 1974 "toward 14.5%" (1980 peak); "$450, not $676" impossible; guy one's $18,000 does not reproduce; "no manager has beaten it" false; dollar reserve share and Treasury size stale. Many 2026 claims SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Not personalised advice. The stored ending is complete.
